tonight.headline: Lost, 103.8 to 140.6. You're 0-3, and Achane's knee is the story now
body: Stafford played Sunday night and Footballers finished on 140.6. Every one of your starters is final at 103.8, so the week is lost and you're 0-3. Monangai plays tonight from your bench, which doesn't count.

Nothing can be set until rosters unlock after tonight's game. The news that matters is Achane's knee: no MRI result had been reported by this snapshot, and every report since Sunday points to a long absence. The Tuten card below is next week's answer; Tuesday's run is the last before claims process at 01:00 Wednesday Mexico City.

case.label: What changed overnight
case.body: Stafford's game pushed Footballers from 119.7 to 140.6 (league file). Jefferson: O'Connell said he doesn't believe the ankle is severe and that Jefferson was 'pretty close to coming back in' (Yahoo/Heavy, 28 Sep). Allen took a helmet to the left knee late and afterwards said 'We're all good' (PFT). Coker's diagnosis is due within 24-48 hours (ClutchPoints).

case.label: Was the lineup wrong?
case.body: No. The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. Three starters were hurt mid-game (Achane, Coker, Jefferson). McLaurin (19.7) and Tuten (17.0) outscored them from the bench, but only hindsight picks those swaps.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing on the scoreboard. Next week depends on Achane's MRI, and on Wednesday's practice reports for Jefferson, Coker and Allen.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: WHEN THE WEEK ROLLS · only if Achane is ruled out or doubtful for Week 4
doFirst.title: If Achane misses Week 4: start Tuten in his RB slot
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed until Miami confirm the MRI, but every report since Sunday points to a long absence. A swap; nobody is dropped.

case.label: The knee
case.body: Achane's left leg was twisted into the turf when a defender caught him from behind (Total Pro Sports). After the game Miami coach Hafley said 'it does not sound very optimistic' and that the team was still gathering information (ESPN's Cameron Wolfe). A sports doctor who reviewed the video raised a possible meniscus injury, and Yahoo's Monday waiver column says it 'should keep him out for a long time if not the rest of the season', pending confirmation. No MRI result had been reported by 12:52 UTC Monday. ESPN has not priced any of this into Week 4.

case.label: Why Tuten
case.body: He's Jacksonville's lead back: 15 carries, 73 yards and a TD on 48% of snaps in a 35-6 win (Florio), with Lawrence throwing three touchdowns (AP). Monangai missed Wednesday and Thursday with a knee before a full Friday (Eagles.com report) and splits Chicago's work with Swift; Kamara shares New Orleans' backfield with Etienne. Next week's projection makes the final call between them.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Rosters unlock after tonight's Bears-Eagles game. The MRI result should land today; Miami's first practice report is Wednesday. Tuesday's run re-checks it.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The MRI is clean and Achane is cleared for Week 4, so the card never fires. If it fires, it's graded on the outcome: the back who starts in Achane's slot against the best bench alternative that week.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: WHEN THE WEEK ROLLS · only if Coker or Jefferson is out for Week 4
doFirst.title: If Coker or Jefferson can't go: McLaurin starts, then Boston
doFirst.subtitle: Not armed, and less likely than it was last night: Minnesota's coach doesn't think Jefferson's ankle is severe. Coker's diagnosis is due within 48 hours.

case.label: The injuries
case.body: Jefferson: O'Connell said 'I don't believe [it's severe]. I just know that he was pretty close to coming back in'; he couldn't get the explosiveness to beat press coverage, and Minnesota planned further evaluation today (Yahoo/Heavy, 28 Sep). Coker: a new quad injury; he said it isn't 'anything too crazy', with an official diagnosis expected within 24-48 hours (ClutchPoints, 27 Sep).

case.label: Why McLaurin
case.body: 9 targets in each of the last two weeks, and 6 for 77 and a TD in Mariota's first start (NBC). Washington GM Adam Peters said Daniels needs no surgery 'as of right now' and there's been no IR talk, with Mariota the starter 'for the foreseeable future' (Bleacher Report, 25 Sep). So the passer is Mariota for now.

case.label: The clock
case.body: Rosters unlock after Monday night. Minnesota and Carolina publish their first practice reports Wednesday.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Both Jefferson and Coker practise fully by Friday, so the card never fires. If it fires, it's graded on the outcome: McLaurin against the receiver he replaced.

whatWentWrong.title: Three starters hurt mid-game
whatWentWrong.lead: Achane (knee), Coker (quad) and Jefferson (ankle). All were started correctly, and together they scored 10.7 on 51.5 projected.

case.label: Not a lineup miss
case.body: The lineup as set was the projection lineup and every starter was active at kickoff. Coker's pregame ankle wasn't what took him out: it was a new quad injury. Achane's was a non-contact knee on his third carry, and Jefferson's a defender landing on his ankle.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Week 4 depends on three medical reports. Achane's already sounds bad; Jefferson's sounds minor (O'Connell, 28 Sep). The two cards above settle the replacements now, so Monday and Wednesday are a checklist.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: All three are cleared for Week 4. Then both cards stay unarmed.

whatWentWrong.sources: CBS Sports · The Big Lead · Yahoo/Heavy · Total Pro Sports

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker-over-McLaurin flex call lost, 3.8 to 19.7
whatWentWrong.lead: Closed WRONG. The falsifier fired: Coker got 4 targets while Mariota threw McLaurin 9.

case.label: The call
case.body: On 21 Sep the brief moved Coker into the flex because Daniels' injury meant Mariota would start. The falsifier said the call was wrong if Coker drew under five targets while McLaurin drew eight or more. Coker got 4 before the quad took him out (The Big Lead). McLaurin got 9 (NBC).

case.label: The honest part
case.body: The injury cut Coker's day short, and that doesn't rescue the call. A lineup decision is graded on its outcome, and this one lost by 15.9. The theory that Mariota would starve McLaurin was wrong on its first test.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The flex slot reopens. Week 4's projection decides it, and the second card makes McLaurin the first replacement if a receiver is out.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: The Week 3 archive disagreeing with the reported target counts. The archive grades it formally on Tuesday.

worthALook.name: Ollie Gordon II
worthALook.ownership: not in the snapshot's wire list
worthALook.lead: Miami's back if Achane is out long-term, which every report since Sunday suggests. Tuesday's decision.

case.label: The role
case.body: After Achane went down in the first quarter, Gordon took over, scored a short touchdown, left with a cramp in the third and came back in the fourth (Heavy). SI's Week 4 wire column has him on 14.5 points and leading the backfield against Minnesota; Yahoo calls him the top add. Jaylen Wright (foot, stinger) was inactive but practised twice and may be back for Week 4 (Heavy).

case.label: Why not a card
case.body: He's not rostered anywhere in Chem, but the snapshot's ~110-player wire list doesn't include him, so I can't see whether he's a free agent or on waivers, or when he'd clear. The waiver tool didn't print him either: it reads Weeks 1-2, and his role began today. Never invent a deadline.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday's run, once the MRI is known: if Achane is out for weeks and Wright is still limited, claim Gordon and drop Kamara, the lowest-projected back. Chem priority resets weekly, so a claim costs nothing lasting. Claims process Wednesday 01:00 Mexico City.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A clean MRI, or Jaylen Wright back at full practice Wednesday, which makes Gordon the RB2 in a committee.

doNotChase.name: Dalton Schultz
doNotChase.lead: The market's right about him, and he still has no place on this roster.

case.body: Nico Collins missed a second straight game (hamstring, ESPN), so Houston's targets run through Schultz. Xavier Hutchinson led their receivers with 3 for 51 in the loss to Indianapolis (SI).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: One TE slot, held by Likely, and a flex that only takes RB or WR. A second TE scores zero here.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Likely being ruled out. Likely had a poor day, but a 3.3 is no reason to replace him.

case.label: The number that kills it

case.label: What would change it

waiverAnalysis.summary: Nothing on the wire beats this roster on usage. Monangai (RB) and Boston (WR) are the weakest players you could move, and nobody on the wire clears either. Two weeks of data is thin, and the tool can't see Sunday: Ollie Gordon's role began after Achane's injury and he isn't in the wire list, so he's a watch row above, not a tool result.
